title: Nicholas Georgescu-Roegen

definition.text: Nicholas Georgescu-Roegen (1906–1994) was a Romanian mathematician, statistician and economist whose work on entropy and natural resources helped found ecological economics.

facts.text: His 1971 book The Entropy Law and the Economic Process argued that all natural resources are irreversibly degraded when used in economic activity.
He described the economy as turning valuable low-entropy resources into worthless high-entropy waste and pollution, which is why resources are scarce.
He argued Earth's carrying capacity will shrink as its finite mineral stock is used up, leading the world economy towards eventual collapse.
By bringing resource flows into economic models, his work was decisive in establishing ecological economics as a separate sub-discipline in the 1980s.
He taught Herman Daly, but later criticised his student's steady-state economy in several articles.
The degrowth movement of the early 2000s treats him as its main intellectual influence.
Mistakes from his incomplete grasp of thermodynamics have caused controversy among physicists and ecological economists.

contested_note: His application of thermodynamics to economics contains mistakes that physicists and ecological economists have argued over.

title: Nicholas Stern
article: Nicholas Stern, Baron Stern of Brentford

definition.text: Nicholas Stern (born 1946) is a British economist, banker and academic who led the Stern Review on the economics of climate change.

facts.text: The Stern Review, produced by his team at HM Treasury, was released in October 2006.
The Review described climate change as an externality, and Stern later called it the greatest market failure the world has seen.
It recommended regulation, carbon taxes, carbon trading, pollution permits and property rights, and urged immediate emission cuts at a significant but manageable cost.
Economists reacted in mixed ways; some called the Review deeply flawed, while others found its conclusions reasonable even if its method was wrong.
He chairs the Grantham Research Institute on Climate Change and the Environment at the London School of Economics.

contested_note: Economists disagreed over the Stern Review, some calling it deeply flawed and others defending its conclusions.
